To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and produced a new pair of cell surface receptors that can induce cell growth in the absence of IL-6 and that this new receptor system is useful for the production of therapeutic proteins.

the use of a binary cell surface receptor composed of a portion of the antibody and a portion of the receptor of the cytokine, in combination with the intracellular domain (the transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains) of the receptor of a different cytokine, enables the production of the target protein in the absence of the original cytokine.

the transfection of a binary cell surface receptor consisting of the anti-lysozyme antibody and the erythrocyte growth factor receptor, gp130, to an interleuken-6-dependent hybrid cell line resulted in the establishment of an inexpensive and stable culture system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of cell culture for the inexpensive propagation and maintenance of mammalian cells.
the design of cell surface receptors that allow the use of inexpensive factors for the growth of mammalian cells in culture.
the design of artificial cell surface receptors for the control of cell growth and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a binary cell surface receptor system, in which the receptor is composed of a ligand-binding portion of an antibody and the intracellular domain from a cytokine receptor, is a useful tool for designing a cell line for inexpensive production of therapeutic products.
the design of artificial cell surface receptors can replace the requirement for costly growth factors, and thus, the use of factor-independent cells is possible.
the use of a cytokine-independent cell line is a viable and practical approach to the production of recombinant proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a binary cytokine-specific receptor is a promising approach for the development of a novel cell engineering technique for the production of recombinant proteins in mammalian cells.

we have succeeded in replacing factor-dependency with factor-independent growth by transfecting a pair of chimeras of the extracellular domain of the anti-HL antibody and the intracellular domain gp130.
the use of cytokines for industrial applications is now feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of cell surface receptors can be applied to tailor cells for inexpensive cell growth.
we can use the receptor design to tailor cell lines for inexpensive induction of cell proliferation for the purpose of making therapeutic proteins.
we can design a cell surface receptor that is capable of binding to an inexpensive ligand to induce cell growth in place of a costly cytokine.
